about: Eval cases for the story pipeline (CLAUDE.md §12). Real cases use Boca Raton releases recorded in packages/adapters/fixtures; synthetic ones are invented to test the safety rules and are marked so. `expect` is what must be true: a skip reason, or tier bounds and whether the story may publish without review. Add the 50 hand-graded Boca stories here as they are graded.

cases.title: City Council adopts Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget
cases.text: The Boca Raton City Council voted 4-1 on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, to adopt the City's Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget of $1,031,450,000, which takes effect Oct. 1, 2026. The adopted operating millage rate is 3.6788 mills, unchanged from the current year. The budget funds 1,812 full-time positions, including six new firefighter-paramedic positions for Boca Raton Fire Rescue Station 8. The capital budget includes $14,200,000 for the resurfacing of Palmetto Park Road between Military Trail and Federal Highway, scheduled to begin in January 2027. Council Member Marc Wigder cast the dissenting vote. The full budget document is available on the City's Financial Services page.

cases.title: Glades Road lane closures for utility work begin Oct. 26
cases.text: The City of Boca Raton Utility Services Department advises that the two eastbound lanes of Glades Road between NW 2nd Avenue and NW 5th Avenue will close from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. nightly, Monday, Oct. 26 through Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, while crews replace a 16-inch water main. One eastbound lane will remain open. Message boards will be placed in advance of the work zone. Drivers are encouraged to use Palmetto Park Road as an alternate route. Questions may be directed to Utility Services at 561-338-7310. Work schedules may change because of weather.

cases.title: Boca Raton Education Advisory Board meets Nov. 4
cases.text: The City of Boca Raton Education Advisory Board will hold its regular meeting on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, at 5:30 p.m. in the Community Room at City Hall, 201 W. Palmetto Park Road. The agenda includes a presentation on the City's after-school program enrollment for the 2026-27 school year, an update on the Boca Raton Innovation Campus internship partnership, and a vote on the board's 2027 meeting calendar. Meetings are open to the public. Residents who wish to speak during public comment may fill out a comment card at the meeting. The agenda will be posted on the City's website at least 72 hours before the meeting.

cases.title: Mayor joins ribbon cutting for new Boca Raton bakery
cases.text: Mayor Andy Thomson joined the owners of Crumb & Co. Bakery for a ribbon cutting on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, at the bakery's new location, 2200 N. Federal Highway, Suite 104. The bakery, owned by Elena and David Moreau, employs 12 people and is open Tuesday through Sunday from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. The City of Boca Raton Office of Economic Development helped the business through the City's Business Ambassador program, which guides new businesses through permitting and licensing. Businesses interested in the program may contact the Office of Economic Development at 561-393-7761.

cases.title: Teen cited after crash on Yamato Road
cases.text: Boca Raton Police Services responded to a two-vehicle crash at Yamato Road and Congress Avenue at 3:15 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026. Police said the driver of a gray sedan, Jordan Ellis, 16, of Boca Raton, was cited for failure to yield. The driver of the second vehicle, a 41-year-old Delray Beach man, was taken to Delray Medical Center with minor injuries. Eastbound Yamato Road was closed for about an hour while officers investigated. Police ask anyone who witnessed the crash to call the Traffic Unit at 561-338-1251. This release is issued by Boca Raton Police Services Public Information Office.

cases.title: Two juveniles arrested in vehicle burglaries
cases.text: Boca Raton Police Services arrested two juveniles on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, in connection with a series of vehicle burglaries in the Boca Square neighborhood. Police said officers responding to a 911 call at 2:40 a.m. found the two near NE 5th Avenue with property reported stolen from three unlocked vehicles. Both were charged with burglary of an unoccupied conveyance and released to their parents. Police are not releasing their names because they are minors. Residents are reminded to lock their vehicles and remove valuables. Anyone with information may call Boca Raton Police Services at 561-338-1234. This release is issued by Boca Raton Police Services Public Information Office.

cases.title: Police arrest man in Mizner Park jewelry store theft
cases.text: Boca Raton Police Services arrested Mark Delaney, 34, of Boca Raton, on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026, in connection with the theft of three watches from a jewelry store in Mizner Park on Oct. 2. Police said Delaney was identified through surveillance video and was arrested without incident at his home in the 900 block of NW 3rd Avenue. He was charged with grand theft and taken to the Palm Beach County Jail. Police said the watches, valued at $18,500, were recovered. The investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information may call Detective Sgt. Ana Ruiz at 561-338-1302. This release is issued by Boca Raton Police Services Public Information Office.

cases.title: Code Compliance board fines property owner over unsafe pool fence
cases.text: The City of Boca Raton Code Compliance Special Magistrate on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026, fined homeowner Linda Park $250 a day, beginning Nov. 1, 2026, if the pool fence at her property in the 1200 block of SW 12th Avenue is not repaired. City inspectors cited the property on Aug. 14, 2026, after finding a broken gate latch and a gap in the fence that did not meet the Florida Building Code's pool barrier requirements. The magistrate gave the owner until Oct. 31 to make repairs. Code Compliance hearings are held monthly at City Hall and are open to the public. Residents may report code concerns through the City's MyBoca app or by calling 561-393-7934.

cases.title: Precautionary boil water notice for part of east Boca Raton
cases.text: The City of Boca Raton Utility Services Department has issued a precautionary boil water notice for customers on NE 20th Street between NE 5th Avenue and Federal Highway, including all addresses on NE 6th Avenue and NE 7th Avenue in that area, after a water main break on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, caused a loss of pressure. As a precaution, affected customers should boil all water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and washing dishes for at least one minute before use. The notice will remain in effect until two consecutive days of bacteriological tests show the water is safe. Customers will be notified when it is lifted. Questions may be directed to Utility Services at 561-338-7310.

cases.title: State inspectors temporarily close downtown restaurant
cases.text: The Florida Division of Hotels and Restaurants ordered Sea Breeze Grill, 101 E. Palmetto Park Road, Boca Raton, to close temporarily on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, after an inspector found 14 violations, including four high-priority violations for rodent activity in the kitchen and food held at unsafe temperatures. The restaurant was allowed to reopen on Saturday, Oct. 10, after a follow-up inspection found the high-priority violations corrected. Inspection reports are public records published by the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation. The City of Boca Raton shares this notice as a public service; the inspection was conducted by the state.

cases.title: Arrest made in sexual battery case
cases.text: Boca Raton Police Services arrested a 29-year-old man on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, on a charge of sexual battery. Police said the victim, a 24-year-old woman who lives in the 400 block of NW 20th Street, reported the assault on Oct. 4, 2026, and identified the suspect. Detectives obtained a warrant after an investigation that included DNA evidence. The suspect was taken to the Palm Beach County Jail. Victim advocates from Boca Raton Police Services are assisting the victim. Anyone with information may call the Special Victims Unit at 561-338-1290. This release is issued by Boca Raton Police Services Public Information Office.

cases.title: Delray Beach opens new splash pad at Pompey Park
cases.text: The City of Delray Beach opened a new splash pad at Pompey Park, 1101 NW 2nd Street, Delray Beach, on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. The $850,000 project was funded by the Delray Beach Community Redevelopment Agency and includes 32 water features, shaded seating and new restrooms. The splash pad is open daily from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. through November and is free to the public. Delray Beach Parks and Recreation Director Sam Metott said the project was the top request from residents in a 2024 survey. For more information, call Delray Beach Parks and Recreation at 561-243-7250.

cases.title: Update on Mizner Park theft case
cases.text: Boca Raton Police Services was notified on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026, that the Office of the State Attorney for the 15th Judicial Circuit has dropped the grand theft charge against Mark Delaney, 34, of Boca Raton, who was arrested Oct. 8 in connection with the theft of watches from a jewelry store in Mizner Park. The State Attorney's Office filed a notice of nolle prosequi. Police said the investigation into the theft remains open. Anyone with information may call Detective Sgt. Ana Ruiz at 561-338-1302. This release is issued by Boca Raton Police Services Public Information Office.
